params.name: opts
params.type: { sceneId?, backend?, runId?, gridSize?, gapMax?, cornerMax?, extMax?, trim? }
params.doc: sceneId defaults to the viewed scene; backend overrides the setting; the rest are engine tolerances

methods.returns: { creates, updates, refusals, lints, log, report } | null
methods.doc: Run the engine on a scene and report what it would build, writing no walls. Not a pure read: it posts a GM-whispered chat card, pings each refusal and prints console tables. One at a time: while preview/run/undo is running, another call warns and returns null.

params.name: opts
params.type: { sceneId?, backend?, runId?, gridSize?, gapMax?, cornerMax?, extMax?, trim? }
params.doc: sceneId defaults to the viewed scene; backend overrides the setting; the rest are engine tolerances

methods.returns: { creates, updates, refusals, lints, log, report } | null
methods.doc: Complete the scene's walls: one update batch (trims/welds), one create batch, then the chat card. Every write is stamped with the run id so undo() can peel it back. One at a time: while preview/run/undo is running, another call warns and returns null.

params.name: opts
params.doc: all: undo every run, not just the latest

sideEffects: flags.pentaryn-walls and flags.wall-autocomplete deleted on restored walls
methods.doc: Undo the latest run on a scene (or all of them): delete the walls it created and restore those it trimmed. Stamps are read under both scopes; a restored wall loses its stamp under each scope it carries. One at a time: while preview/run/undo is running, another call warns and returns null.
Create (or reuse) the 'Walls: <action>' script macro and put it on the hotbar.
